Duration of the Petition Year/s Month/s Day/s  01 03 15  JUDGMENT

The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- for the accidental injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident took place on 06.10.2023.

2. The Brief facts of the petitioner's case is as under:
It is the case of the petitioner that on 06.10.2023 at about 09.20 p.m., the petitioner was riding motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-42-U-9805 along with pillion rider slowly and cautiously by following all traffic rules and regulations and by observing om moving vehicles and by wearing head guard on Mahadevapura Service Road, at that time one Car bearing Reg. No.KA-04-AC-6903 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner endangering to human life came to main road at a high speed and dashed against the petitioner's Scooter bearing Reg. No. KA-53-HB-3035 and the said Scooter came and dashed against petitioner's motorcycle.
Due to forced impact, petitioner and pillion rider both fell down and petitioner sustained grevious injuries and pillion rider sustained simple injuries.

Immediately, petitioner was shifted to MTB Orthopaedic & Trauma Hospital, Bangalore, wherein he was treated as inpatient and petitioner has spent more than Rs.3,50,000/- towards medical expenses, conveyance, nourishment and conveyance charges.
The petitioner further submitted that, prior to the accident he was heal and healthy and aged about 44 years, the petitioner was working as delivery boy and earning a sum of Rs.30,000/- p.m.
Due to the injuries sustained in the accident the petitioner has become permanently disabled and unable to look after the said work.
Respondent No.1 is the owner of the offending vehicle and Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner has filed this petition for a compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- with interest.
3. After service of notice, both the respondents appeared through their counsels and filed written statements separately.

The respondent No.1 in his written statement denied the allegations made in the plaint and Sunil S M vs Annaiah Shivashankar on 17 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154932424/
2 submitted that, the petitioner only riding his vehicles recklessly but also talking to his friend who was also riding scooter bearing Reg. No. KA-53-HB-3035.

entities.text: Sunil S M vs Annaiah Shivashankar
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: At that point of time the scooter rider bearing Reg. No. KA-53-HB-3035 stated supra has suddenly came to the middle of the road without observing the vehicle coming from opposite side i.e., swift car bearing Reg. No. KA-04-AC-6903 belong to this respondent and driven by its driver.
Though the driver of the car tried to avoid hitting the scooter by applying the brake, he could not suddenly control the vehicle and hit the scooter.
The said scooter in turn hit the motorcycle of the petitioner and due to the said impact both rider and the pillion fell down.
Hence, the said accident has occurred due to the reckless and careless driving of both scooter and motorcycle rider.

The respondent No.2 in its written statement denied the allegations made in the plaint and submitted that, this respondent issued the policy to the offending car and liability if any is subjected to the terms and conditions of the policy.

Further, this respondent submitted that, the petitioner/rider of the Hero Passion motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-42-U-9805 was riding the same without having valid driving license and insurance in a rash and negligent manner with high speed and has not exercised proper care and caution and himself fallen on road and sustained injuries and he has suffered self negligence of self-accident.

Further, this respondent submitted that,
this petition is bad for mis-joinder of necessary parties.

Further, this respondent submitted that, the facts have been twisted and given wrong description and a false charge-sheet has been made against the alleged driver of the alleged Car bearing Reg. No. KA-04-AC-6903.
Further, the alleged car is commercial vehicle and it was plying without valid permit as on the date of accident.
Further, this respondent seeks protection u/s 170, 134(c), 158(6) of M. V. Act.
Further both the respondent denied the age, occupation and income of the petitioner.
The petitioner colluding with the police filed the false case.
By these reasons, it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

4. On the basis of above pleadings, my learned predecessor framed the following issues are as under:
1. Whether the petitioner proves that, on 06.01.2023 at about 09.20 p.m., near Mahadevapura service road, he met with accident and sustained grievous injuries due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Car bearing Reg. No. KA-04- AC-6903?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation?
If so, how much and from whom?

3. What order or Award?
5. In order to prove the case of the petitioner, he has got himself examined as P.W.1 and got marked documents at Ex.P.1 to P.14 and examined one Srinath.K as PW.2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.15 and Ex.P.16 and also examined Dr. S. Ramachandra as PW.3 and got marked the documents at Ex.P.17 and Ex.P.18 and closed their side.
On the other hand, GPA Holder of respondent No.1 is examined as RW.1 and got marked a document at Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.4.

sentences.text: 6. Heard arguments of both the sides and perused the materials placed on record.
7. My findings on the above issues are as under; Issue No.1: In the Affirmative, Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative.
Issue No.3: As per final order, for the following:
:REASONS:

8. ISSUE No.1: The petitioner has contended that on the above said date, time and place he met with accident and sustained grievous injuries occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of offending vehicle.
9. The petitioner who is injured in this accident has got examined himself as PW-1 by reiterating the averments made in the petition.
He has produced the documents at Ex.P.1 to 14.

Ex.P.1 is the FIR,
Ex.P2 is the complaint, Ex.P.3 is the charge-sheet, Ex.P.4 is the spot mahazar, Ex.P.5 is the Sketch,

Ex.P.6 is the IMV Report, Ex.P.7 is the Wound certificate, Ex.P.8 is the notice u/s 133 of M. V. Act,
Ex.P.9 is the Reply notice, Ex.P.10 is the police intimation, Ex.P.11 is the Discharge Summary,
Ex.P.12 is the Notarized copy of Aadhar Card, Ex.P.13 is the Notarized copy of Driving License and Ex.P.14 is the medical bills.

10. On going through the materials, it could be seen that on 06.10.2023 at about 09.20 p.m., the petitioner was riding motorcycle bearing Reg. No.KA-42-U-9805 along with pillion rider slowly and cautiously by following all traffic rules and regulations and by observing om moving vehicles and by wearing head guard on Mahadevapura Service Road, at that time one Car bearing Reg.
No.KA-04-AC-6903 driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner endangering to human life came to main road at a high speed and dashed against the petitioner's Scooter bearing Reg. No.
KA-53-HB-3035 and the said Scooter came and dashed against petitioner's motorcycle.
Due to forced impact, petitioner and pillion rider both fell down and petitioner sustained grevious injuries and pillion rider sustained simple injuries.
Immediately, petitioner was shifted to MTB Orthopaedic & Trauma Hospital, Bangalore, wherein he was treated as inpatient.
Accordingly, the Mahadevapura Traffic Police have registered a case in Cr.No.182/2023.

After completion of the investigation, the Investigating Officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offences punishable U/s 279 and 338 of IPC.
11.
The negligence in common parlance means and simply failure to exercise due care, expected of a reasonable prudent person.
It is a breach of duty and negligence in law ranging from an advertence to shameful disregard of safety of others.
In most instances, it is caused or heedlessness or inadvertence, by which the negligent party is unaware of the results, which may follow from his act.
Negligence is that, a breach of duty or lack of probable care in doing something.
In short, it is want of attention and doing of something, which a prudent and reasonable man would not do.
The burden is upon the petitioner to prove that, the accident occurred due to negligent driving of the driver of Car bearing Reg. No. KA-53-HB-3035.

sentences.text: As we know evidence in any Summary Proceedings, "The act of Negligence" will have to be assessed on the basis of broad preponderance of probabilities and degree of proof required is not one of beyond reasonable doubt, as it is insisted in criminal case for "The Negligent Act".
13. The certified copy of the First Information (First information statement/s complaint in common para-lace) lodged before the Mahadevapura Traffic Police has been marked as Ex.P2.
On receiving the First Information, the Station House Officer chose to register a case in Crime No. 182/2023.

The said certified copy of First Information Report (F.I.R.) is marked as Ex.P1.
14.

During the Course of examination-in-chief, he got marked Ex.P1 to 10 are the only documents,
which are to be scrutinized to arrive at conclusion- whether the accident was owing to the negligent manner of driving of driver of offending car.

The Ex.P.4 (spot panchanama) and Ex.P.5 (Sketch),
clearly discloses the place of accident and that the police, after registering the First Information,
held investigation and filed the Ex.P.3, Charge-Sheet against the rider of motorcycle U/s. 279 and 338 of IPC.
The Ex.P.6 i.e., certified copy of the IMV Report discloses that, the accident was not occurred due to any mechanical defects of the vehicle in question.

15. On the other hand, respondent No.1 examined his GPA Holder as RW.1, who depose that, the petitioner was riding motorcycle bearing Reg. No. KA-42-U-9805 along with the pillion rider in a rash and negligent manner without caring for the traffic rules and regulations and riding without keeping in mind the ongoing vehicles.

He further depose that, the petitioner not only riding his vehicle recklessly but also talking to his friend who was also riding scooter bearing Reg. No.
KA-53-HB-3035, at that time scooter rider suddenly came to the middle of the road without observing the vehicle coming from opposite side and driver of offending car tried to avoid hitting the scooter by applying the brake, he could not suddenly control the vehicle and hit the scooter, the said scooter in turn hit the motorcycle of the petitioner.
Hence, this accident occurred due to reckless and careless driving of both scooter and motorcycle rider.
16. Contesting respondents have not disputed the accident.
The counsel for insurance company has taken contention that, the accident is taken place due to self negligence of petitioner.
In support of his contention he relied upon the hand sketch map at Ex.P.5.

On perusal of Ex.P.5 it reveals that,
accident is taken place at the middle of the road.
However, that does not mean that, accident is caused due to the negligence of petitioner himself.
On the other hand, as stated above, I.O has filed charge-sheet against the rider of the 4-wheeler vehicle for the offence punishable u/s 279 and 338 of IPC.
Except suggestions and denial insurance company has not produced any documents to show that, accident is also caused due to the negligence of petitioner also.

17. In a claim of compensation U/s.166 of M. V. Act 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Honble Apex Court in Kusum and others Vs. Satveer and others reported in 2011 SAR (CIVIL) 319.

18. In view of the detailed discussion held above, I am of the opinion that, the petitioner has proved negligence on the part of driver of the offending vehicle and as such the accident in question had Sunil S M vs Annaiah Shivashankar on 17 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154932424/

sentences.text: By relying on evidence of P.W.1 and the Police records, I am of the considered view that the accident in question took place due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the Car bearing Reg. No. KA-53-HB-3035.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 in the affirmative.
19. ISSUE No.2:
The petitioner in his evidence has specifically deposed that, after the accident he was shifted to MTB Hospital, wherein he was admitted as inpatient and took treatment.
Petitioner has stated in the petition that, he is undergoing deep mental shock, severe pain and sufferings.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads:
20. PAIN AND SUFFERING:

In the petition as well as in his evidence PW1 deposed that,
immediately after the accident he was shifted to MTB Hospital, wherein he was admitted as inpatient from 06.10.2023 to 09.10.2023.
The petitioner has produced the discharge summary marked at Ex.P.11 wherein it is mentioned that the petitioner was admitted in the MTB Orthopedic & Trauma Hospital, Bangalore for 03 days.

He has produced the wound certificate marked at Ex.P.7,
which reveals that, petitioner has sustained Fracture shaft of left tibia and fibula and the doctor has opined that the injury is grievous in nature.
Hence, it is clear that during the above said period the petitioner suffered lot of pain and inconvenience.
Considering all these aspects this tribunal has granted Rs.50,000/- under the head of pain and suffering.
21. MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The petitioner has pleaded in the petition that he has spent huge amount towards medical expenses.
In support of his plea, he has produced 08 medical bills which are marked at Ex.P.14 to the tune of Rs.1,60,000/-.
Hence, looking to the injuries sustained and treatment taken by the petitioner.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,60,000/-
towards medical expenses.

22. LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID UP PERIOD:
The petitioner has produced Ex.P.11 Discharge summary issued by MTB Orthopedic & Trauma Hospital, Bangalore, it reveals that, the petitioner took treatment from the said hospital from 06.10.2023 to 09.10.2023 i.e., for 03 days.
Hence, at least 2 months is required to recover from the accidental injuries.
It is the further contended that, the injured petitioner was delivery boy and earning Rs.35,000/- per month, in support of his income he has not produced any single document.

So, in the absence of any evidence in respect of the income of the petitioner, the petitioner might have monthly income at Rs.16,000/- as per the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka fixed notional income of the year 2023 at Rs.16,000/- per month for determination of income before Lok-Adalat for the Districts coming under the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Bengaluru Bench.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The accident is of the year is 2023.
Hence, the income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.16,000/-p.m. as per above decision.
Hence, 2 months is to be considered as loss of income.
Hence, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.32,000/- under this head.

23. Towards loss of future earning capacity on account of Permanent Physical Disability- Sunil S M vs Annaiah Shivashankar on 17 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154932424/

sentences.text: The petitioner to prove her disability, he has produced the evidence of Dr. S. Ramachandra in order to substantiate the same, PW.3 who has opined that, total physical disability of 36.16% and that of whole body disability at 18.08%.
Admittedly, the PW.3 is not a treated doctor.

Same was admitted by the PW.3 during his cross examination, the relevant evidence of the PW.3 reads as follows :
"I am not a treated doctor.
I have no personal knowledge about the treatment given to the petitioner."
He was sworn that, petitioner has got 18.08% disability to the whole body but he was not issued the disability certificate.
It is quite but natural that to help the petitioner doctor will give exaggerated disability.
However, looking to the nature of the injuries it is proper to came to conclusion that there is 11% of disability to the petitioner.
24. Before proceeding on merits of the claim the age of the petitioner /injured has to be determined.
Ex.P.12 is the Aadhar Card of the petitioner, wherein his DOB is mentioned as 10.12.1994 and accident took place in the year 2023.
Accordingly, I assess her age as 29 years at the time of this accident.
As per the ruling reported in AIR 2009 SCW page-3014 between SARLA VERAMA AND OTHERS VS DELHI TRANSPORT CORPORATION AND OTHERS, the relevant multiplier applicable is '17'.

Under this head the petitioner is entitled for an amount of Rs.3,59,040/-.
25.
FOOD, CONVEYANCE, NOURISHMENT AND ATTENDANT CHARGES:
Further the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and took treatment as inpatient in MTB Orthopedic and Trauma Hospital, Bangalore as inpatient from 06.10.2023 to 09.10.2023 i.e., for 03 days.

entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
Hence, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.30,000/-
under the head of nutritious food and attendant charges.
26. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
The petitioner was aged about 29 years at the time of accident, he has sustained grievous injuries.
It shows that he found difficulty in doing day to day works.
He might have suffered lot of pain and loss of amenities and comforts in life.
Therefore, considering the age, nature of injuries and percentage of disability, Rs.20,000/- is awarded under the head of loss of future amenities and happiness.
27. TOWARDS FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES :
The petitioner has claimed towards future medical expenses.
The doctor who has been examined as PW.2 has suggested for removal of the implants from Tibia of left leg.
By keeping nature of the injuries sustained, as he is bound to suffer medical problems in future and cannot every time depend upon Government hospital.
Hence, under this head Rs.30,000/- is awarded.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation under the following heads:
1 Pain and sufferings Rs. 50,000/-

loss of happiness.

Total Rs. 6,71,040/-
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.6,71,040/- under various heads.
28. LIABILITY:

As discussed in Issue No.1, the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Car bearing Reg. No.KA-04-AC-6903 and the police have conducted due enquiry and filed charge sheet against the said driver of the offending vehicle.
From perusal of the policy, the offending vehicle was insured with the respondent No.2 for the period from 03.06.2023 to 02.06.2024.
Admittedly, the accident in question took place on 06.10.2023.
Hence, policy was in force at the time of accident.
Hence, in view of above discussion, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
However, respondent No.2 being the insurer is liable to indemnify the respondent No.1 owner.
29. INTEREST:

As far as awarding of interest on the compensation amount is concerned, I have relied on a decision reported in M.F.A. No.100090 of 2014 in between Vijay Ishwar Jadhav and others V/s The Divisional Manager, Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Co. Ltd, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has awarded interest at the rate of 6%.

By relying on the aforesaid decision,
6% interest awarded to the petitioners in the present case on hand.
Accordingly, issue No.3 is answered partly in the affirmative.
30. ISSUE No.4:

In view of above discussions, I proceed to pass the following:
:ORDER:
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of I.M.V Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is awarded with compensation of Rs.6,71,040/- with interest @ 6%

Remaining 50% of compensation amount of  petitioner in total compensation amount including interest thereon shall be deposited in his name as F.D. in any of the Nationalized or Scheduled Bank as per choice of petitioner for a period of two years.

2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Circular No.2/2019 dated:19.08.2019.

In case of deposit of awarded amount, the petitioner is entitled to receive amount as mentioned above after expiry of period provided for filing an appeal.

Bank shall release amount along with interest thereon in favour of petitioner after expiry of two years period of deposit on proper verification and identification,
without waiting for further order of court.

Draw award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The petitioner has filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicle Act, claiming compensation of Rs.25,00,000/- for the accidental injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident took place on 06.10.2023.
Due to forced impact, petitioner and pillion rider both fell down and petitioner sustained grevious injuries and pillion rider sustained simple injuries.
Hence, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Further, this respondent seeks protection u/s 170, 134(c), 158(6) of M. V. Act.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Due to forced impact, petitioner and pillion rider both fell down and petitioner sustained grevious injuries and pillion rider sustained simple injuries.
Immediately, petitioner was shifted to MTB Orthopaedic & Trauma Hospital, Bangalore, wherein he was treated as inpatient.
Accordingly, the Mahadevapura Traffic Police have registered a case in Cr.No.182/2023.
After completion of the investigation, the Investigating Officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offences punishable U/s 279 and 338 of IPC.
11.
The negligence in common parlance means and simply failure to exercise due care, expected of a reasonable prudent person.
It is a breach of duty and negligence in law ranging from an advertence to shameful disregard of safety of others.
In most instances, it is caused or heedlessness or inadvertence, by which the negligent party is unaware of the results, which may follow from his act.
Negligence is that, a breach of duty or lack of probable care in doing something.
In short, it is want of attention and doing of something, which a prudent and reasonable man would not do.
The burden is upon the petitioner to prove that, the accident occurred due to negligent driving of the driver of Car bearing Reg. No. KA-53-HB-3035.

30. ISSUE No.4:
In view of above discussions, I proceed to pass the following:
:ORDER:
The petition filed by the Petitioner under Sec.166 of I.M.V Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.
The petitioner is awarded with compensation of Rs.6,71,040/- with interest @ 6%
p.a., on Rs.6,41,040/- (excluding future medical expenses of Rs.30,000/-) from the Sunil S M vs Annaiah Shivashankar on 17 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/154932424/
8 date of petition till its realization.
The respondent No.2 being insurer of the vehicle involved in an accident is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.
Respondent No.2 is directed to deposit the above compensation amount with interest thereon before Tribunal within two months from the date of this award.
In the event of deposit of total compensation amount of petitioner, 50% of amount shall be released in his favour along with interest thereon.
Remaining 50% of compensation amount of  petitioner in total compensation amount including interest thereon shall be deposited in his name as F.D. in any of the Nationalized or Scheduled Bank as per choice of petitioner for a period of two years.
After deposit of compensation amount with interest thereon, disburse amount as mentioned above as per guidelines laid down by Hon'ble High Court in MFA No.
2509/2019 (ECA) and as per General Circular No.2/2019 dated:19.08.2019.
The petitioner is hereby directed to produce particulars of his Bank Account, with name of Bank, IFSC Code, Account Number with copy of First Page of Bank Pass Book which contains compulsorily photograph of petitioner, which is duly attested by concerned Bank.
Further petitioner shall produce PAN Card/Aadhar Card.
In case of deposit of awarded amount, the petitioner is entitled to receive amount as mentioned above after expiry of period provided for filing an appeal.
Bank shall not advance loan on such FD, and shall not cause premature release of FD without permission by the Tribunal.
Bank shall release amount along with interest thereon in favour of petitioner after expiry of two years period of deposit on proper verification and identification,
without waiting for further order of court.
The advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
